headline: Files by Google lacks multi-cloud and dual-pane view, features common in other file managers
summary: Despite its simplicity, Files by Google falls short on essential features like broad cloud storage integration and a dual-pane view, making file management cumbersome.
details: Files by Google, a staple on Google Pixel phones, is criticized for missing two crucial features: extensive cloud storage compatibility and a dual-pane view. While its simplicity is appealing, these limitations force users to juggle multiple apps for efficient file management.

The app's biggest drawback is its limited cloud integration. While it offers straightforward backup to Google Drive, accessing other services like Dropbox is clunky, requiring users to share files rather than directly integrating them from a file's drop-down menu.

Many third-party file managers, including Samsung's My Files and Solid Explorer, offer broader cloud support. Users desire the ability to select any cloud storage service directly from a file's options, mirroring a common and useful feature found elsewhere.
Another significant omission is the lack of a dual-pane view. Files by Google only shows a single window at a time, making moving files between folders a laborious process of flipping back and forth.

Apps like Solid Explorer offer side-by-side independent windows in landscape mode, allowing users to drag and drop files between source and destination folders. This functionality significantly simplifies file organization, especially when managing numerous files.

This dual-pane functionality is particularly critical on foldable phones, where the large screen space could be utilized for efficient multi-folder management. Its absence makes Files by Google feel outdated on modern devices like the Pixel 11 Pro Fold.

Despite these shortcomings, Files by Google excels in its storage saver tools. It efficiently detects old screenshots, duplicate images, large videos, and junk files, allowing users to clear out gigabytes of space with just a few taps.

The ubiquity of multi-cloud support and dual-pane viewing in competitor apps highlights the urgent need for Files by Google to integrate these features. Users seek a single, comprehensive app for viewing, managing, and cleaning up space, rather than relying on multiple third-party solutions.

headline_marked: [[Claude Code AI agent found a crypto miner]] using 1175% CPU on a developer's overheating Mac
headline: Claude Code AI agent found a crypto miner using 1175% CPU on a developer's overheating Mac
summary: An AI coding assistant detected xmrig, a crypto miner, hogging 12 CPU cores and causing temperatures to hit 112°C on a Mac, explaining the machine's poor performance.
details: A developer's Mac was found to be running a crypto miner, xmrig, which was consuming an astonishing 1175% CPU across roughly 12 cores. The AI coding agent, Claude Code, flagged the issue while assisting the developer with a temperature monitor app, explaining the Mac's severe performance degradation.

The cryptomining malware was likely added to the Mac's startup processes on August 29. The developer, known as UntilHEX on Reddit, was prompted to create a temperature monitoring app specifically to diagnose why their computer was running so hot.

Claude intervened after UntilHEX noticed unusually high raw temperature sensor readings, with the CPU peaking at a very toasty 112 degrees Celsius. The AI accurately identified the sustained heavy load from xmrig as the cause of the extreme heat.

The AI agent then detailed how the crypto miner had hidden itself and was running at startup on the Apple Silicon computer. Claude cautiously offered to clean up the CPU-hogging software, suggesting it would stop the startup item, halt the miner, and move the files to a quarantine folder.

UntilHEX confirmed that Claude was tasked with the cleanup, which proved highly effective, requiring only one manual file deletion due to an access issue. A subsequent Malwarebytes scan verified the AI's successful removal of the unwanted crypto miner software.
